paragraphs: GLPI is a self-administered and self-managed Pennsylvania REIT. GLPI was incorporated on February 13, 2013, as a wholly-owned subsidiary of PENN Entertainment, Inc., formerly known as Penn National Gaming, Inc. (NASDAQ: PENN) ("PENN"). On November 1, 2013, PENN contributed to the Company, through a series of internal corporate restructurings, substantially all of the assets and liabilities associated with PENN's real property interests and real estate development business, as well as the assets and liabilities of Hollywood Casino Baton Rouge and Hollywood Casino Perryville (which are referred to as the "TRS Properties") and then spun-off GLPI to holders of PENN's common and preferred stock in a tax-free distribution (the "Spin-Off").

Since 2021, the Company has been structured as an umbrella partnership REIT under which substantially all of its business is conducted through GLP Capital, L.P. ("GLP Capital"), the day-to-day management of which is exclusively controlled by GLPI. GLPI has no material assets other than its investment in GLP Capital. GLPI issues equity from time to time and is obligated to contribute the net proceeds from those offerings to GLP Capital. As of December 31, 2025, GLPI owned 97.1% of the outstanding units of GLP Capital with the remaining units owned by third party limited partners who (directly or through affiliates) contributed properties to GLP Capital in exchange for consideration that was partially funded through the issuance of operating partnership units ("OP Units") and holders of long term incentive plan units ("LTIP Units"). The OP Units and LTIP Units once vested are exchangeable on a one for one basis for common shares of the Company. The Company's common stock is listed on the NASDAQ under the ticker symbol GLPI.

All debt of the Company, including revolving credit facilities, term loans and senior unsecured notes, is incurred by GLP Capital and its subsidiaries. GLPI has fully and unconditionally guaranteed all of the Company's outstanding debt obligations.

The Company seeks to provide an opportunity to invest in the growth opportunities afforded by the gaming industry, with the stability and cash flow opportunities of a REIT. GLPI's primary business consists of acquiring, financing, and owning real estate property to be leased to gaming operators in triple-net lease arrangements. The Company also extends loans that produce fixed or variable returns which may convert into leased rent upon project completion or stabilization.

As of December 31, 2025, GLPI's portfolio consisted of interests in 69 gaming and related facilities, including the real property associated with 34 gaming and related facilities operated by PENN, the real property associated with 6 gaming and related facilities operated by Caesars Entertainment (NASDAQ: CZR) ("Caesars"), the real property associated with 4 gaming and related facilities operated by Boyd Gaming Corporation (NYSE: BYD) ("Boyd"), the real property associated with 15 gaming and related facilities operated by Bally's Corporation (NYSE: BALY) ("Bally's") and 1 facility under development namely Bally's Chicago, the real property associated with 3 gaming and related facilities operated by The Cordish Companies ("Cordish"), 1 gaming facility managed by a subsidiary of Hard Rock International ("Hard Rock"), 4 gaming and related facilities operated by Strategic Gaming Management, LLC ("Strategic") and 1 gaming and related facility operated by American Racing & Entertainment, LLC ("American Racing"). These facilities, including our corporate headquarters building, are geographically diversified across 20 states and we own over 5,600 acres and lease approximately 1,000 acres. As of December 31, 2025, our properties were 100% occupied. GLPI expects to continue growing its portfolio by pursuing opportunities to acquire or develop additional gaming facilities to lease to gaming operators under prudent terms.
We believe the following competitive strengths will contribute significantly to our success:
Geographically Diverse Property Portfolio

We seek to expand our portfolio by working with multiple tenants in different jurisdictions. We are focused primarily on regional gaming markets where customers are less dependent on air travel and where demand has historically been resilient. As of December 31, 2025, our portfolio consisted of 69 gaming and related facilities. Our portfolio, including our corporate headquarters building, is comprised of approximately 6,600 acres of land and is broadly diversified by location across 20 states which we expect to expand to 22 states our recently announced transactions in California and Virginia. We expect that our geographic diversification will limit the effect of a decline in any one regional market on our overall performance.

Approximately 97% of our cash rent comes from five of the company's tenants, PENN, Caesars, Boyd, Cordish and Bally's, that are leading, diversified, multi-jurisdictional owners and managers of gaming and pari-mutuel properties and established gaming providers. With the exception of Cordish, all of the aforementioned tenants are publicly traded companies that are subject to the informational filing requirements of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, and are required to file periodic reports on Form 10-K and Form 10-Q and current reports on Form 8-K with the Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC"). Readers are directed to PENN's, Caesars, Boyd's and Bally's respective websites for further financial information on these companies.

Our real estate properties are leased under long-term triple-net leases guaranteed by our tenants, pursuant to which the tenant is responsible for all facility maintenance, insurance required in connection with the leased properties and the business conducted on the leased properties, including coverage of the landlord's interests, taxes levied on or with respect to the leased properties (other than taxes on our income) and all utilities and other services necessary or appropriate for the leased properties and the business conducted on the leased properties. Our leases include fixed escalators, escalators that are subject to the attainment of certain rent coverage ratios and other contractual rent growth features such as those linked to the Consumer Price Index ("CPI") with floors and ceilings.
Resilient Regional Gaming Characteristics

The Company's asset portfolio is composed primarily of regional, drive-to gaming properties rather than destination resorts. Historically, regional gaming properties have demonstrated lower performance volatility as compared to destination resort casinos. Additionally, given lower capex burdens, regional gaming assets often prove to be more stable cash flowing assets when compared to destination resorts, under similar rent structure dynamics. Furthermore, we believe that the recession resulting from the COVID-19 pandemic has illustrated the resiliency of the regional gaming market. In spite of all our properties being mandated to close during mid-March 2020, the Company received all contractual rents, inclusive of rent credits, due in 2020. We believe that our assets should generate substantial cash flows well into the future for both ourselves and our tenants.
Embedded growth through funding commitments

The Company grows through contractual escalations in our leases as well as acquisitions and fundings for development projects. Since January 1, 2024, we have completed transactions totaling $3.7 billion. See footnote 11 in the Notes to the financial statements for listing of the various funding commitments that are expected to contribute to future growth opportunities for the Company.

headings: Risk Factors Relating to Our Business
The bankruptcy or insolvency of any of our tenants could result in termination of such tenant's lease and material losses to us.
Our pursuit of investments in, and acquisitions or development of, additional properties may be unsuccessful or fail to meet our expectations.
We are dependent on the gaming industry and may be susceptible to the risks associated with it, which could materially adversely affect our business, financial position or results of operations.
Certain of our tenants operate and manage facilities that are located in areas that experience extreme weather conditions and are more sensitive to the adverse effects of climate change.
We face extensive regulation from gaming and other regulatory authorities.
Required regulatory approvals can delay or prohibit transfers of our gaming properties, which could result in periods in which we are unable to receive rent for such properties.
Our agreements to provide funding for various casino development projects expose us to risks of loss that are different from those associated with the ownership and leasing of properties.
We might not be able to exercise customary enforcement rights as the lender under our tribal loans.
Our pursuit of strategic acquisitions unrelated to the gaming industry may be unsuccessful or fail to meet our expectations.
Environmental compliance costs and liabilities associated with real estate properties owned by us may materially impair the value of those investments.

We face risks associated with security breaches through cyber-attacks, cyber intrusions or otherwise, as well as other significant disruptions of our information technology (IT) networks and related systems.
We face certain risks related to our properties that are subject to ground and use lease arrangements.
Uncertainty regarding and changes in U.S. trade policies and tariffs may increase costs and adversely affect our tenants', and, therefore, our financial condition.
Our success depends on our ability to attract, motivate and retain key personnel and plan for future executive transitions.
Risk Factors Relating to our Status as a REIT
Qualifying as a REIT involves highly technical and complex provisions of the Code and violations of these provisions could jeopardize our REIT qualifications.
We could fail to qualify to be taxed as a REIT if income we receive from our tenants, or their subsidiaries, is not treated as qualifying income.
Dividends payable by REITs do not qualify for the reduced tax rates available for some dividends.
Changes to U.S. federal income tax laws could materially and adversely affect us and our shareholders.
REIT distribution requirements could adversely affect our ability to execute our business plan.
Even if we remain qualified as a REIT, we may face other tax liabilities that reduce our cash flow.
Complying with REIT requirements may cause us to forego otherwise attractive acquisition opportunities or liquidate otherwise attractive investments.
Complying with REIT requirements may limit our ability to hedge effectively and may cause us to incur tax liabilities.
Our charter restricts the ownership and transfer of our outstanding stock, which may have the effect of delaying, deferring or preventing a transaction or change of control of our company.
Risks Related to Our Capital Structure
We have a material amount of indebtedness which could have a significant effect on our business.
paragraphs: The majority of our revenues are dependent on PENN and its subsidiaries. Any event that has a material adverse effect on PENN's business, financial position or results of operations may have a material adverse effect on our business, financial position or results of operations.

The majority of our revenue is based on the revenue derived under our master leases with subsidiaries of PENN. Because these master leases are triple-net leases, we depend on PENN to operate the properties that we own in a manner that generates revenues sufficient to allow PENN to meet its obligations to us, including payment of rent and all insurance, taxes, utilities and maintenance and repair expenses, and to indemnify, defend and hold us harmless from and against various claims, litigation and liabilities arising in connection with its business. There can be no assurance that PENN will have sufficient assets, income or access to financing to enable it to satisfy its payment obligations to us under the master leases. The ability of PENN to fulfill its obligations depends, in part, upon the overall profitability of its gaming operations and, other than limited contractual protections afforded to us as a landlord, we have no control over PENN or its operations. The inability or unwillingness of PENN to meet its subsidiaries' rent obligations and other obligations under the master leases may materially and adversely affect our business, financial position or results of operations, including our ability to pay dividends to our shareholders.

Due to our dependence on rental payments from PENN as a significant source of revenue, we may be limited in our ability to enforce our rights under the master leases. Failure by PENN to comply with the terms of its master leases or to comply with the gaming regulations to which the leased properties are subject could require us to find another lessee for such leased property. In such event, we may be unable to locate a suitable lessee at similar rental rates or at all, which would have the effect of reducing our rental revenues. Likewise, our financial position may be materially weakened if PENN failed to renew or extend any master lease as such lease expires and we are unable to lease or re-lease our properties on economically favorable terms.

Any event that has a material adverse effect on PENN's business, financial position or results of operations, including a corporate change in control event or a material change in the composition of PENN's board of directors could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial position or results of operations. In addition, continued consolidation in the gaming industry would increase our dependence on our existing tenants and could make it increasingly difficult for us to find alternative tenants for our properties.

The bankruptcy or insolvency of any of our tenants could diminish the income we receive from that tenant's lease or leases. If a tenant becomes bankrupt or insolvent, federal law may prohibit us from evicting such tenant based solely upon such bankruptcy or insolvency. In addition, a bankrupt or insolvent tenant may be authorized to reject and terminate its lease or leases with us. Any claims against such bankrupt tenant for unpaid future rent would be subject to statutory limitations that would likely result in our receipt of rental revenues that are substantially less than the contractually specified rent we are owed under the lease or leases. In addition, any claim we have for unpaid past rent may not be paid in full. We may also be unable to re-lease a terminated or rejected space or to re-lease it on comparable or more favorable terms. Moreover, tenants who are considering filing for bankruptcy protection may request amendments of their master leases to remove certain of the properties they lease from us under such master leases. We cannot guarantee that we will be able to sell or re-lease such properties or that lease termination fees, if any, received in exchange for such releases will be sufficient to make up for the rental revenues lost as a result of such lease amendments.

We operate in a highly competitive industry and face competition from other REITs (including other gaming-focused REITs), investment companies, private equity and hedge fund investors, sovereign funds, lenders, gaming companies and other investors, some of whom are significantly larger and have greater resources and lower costs of capital. Increased competition may make it more challenging to identify and successfully capitalize on acquisition opportunities that meet our investment objectives. If we cannot identify and acquire a sufficient number of investment properties at favorable prices or if we are unable to finance acquisitions on commercially favorable terms, our business, financial position or results of operations could be materially adversely affected. Additionally, the fact that we must distribute 90% of our net taxable income in order to maintain our qualification as a REIT may limit our ability to rely upon rental payments from our leased properties or subsequently acquired properties in order to finance acquisitions. As a result, if debt or equity financing is not available on acceptable terms, further acquisitions might be limited or curtailed and completing proposed acquisitions may be adversely impacted. Furthermore, fluctuations in the price of our common stock may impact our ability to finance additional acquisitions through the issuance of common stock and/or cause significant dilution.

paragraphs: We reported total revenues and income from operations of $1,594.8 million and $1,201.5 million, respectively, for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to $1,531.5 million and $1,130.7 million, respectively, for the year ended December 31, 2024. The major factors affecting our results for the year ended December 31, 2025, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, were as follows:

•Total income from real estate was $1,594.8 million and $1,531.5 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. Total income from real estate increased by $63.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024. The reason for the increase was primarily due to our recent acquisitions and development activity which in the aggregate increased cash income by $73.6 million. Current year results also benefited by $17.7 million from escalations on our leases and higher percentage rent of $2.3 million. The Company also recognized unfavorable straight-line and deferred rent adjustments of $33.6 million compared to the corresponding period in the prior year, as well as lower accretion of $0.6 million on its Investment in leases. Finally, the Company had higher ground rent income of $3.9 million.

•Total operating expenses decreased by $7.6 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, as compared to the prior year. The provision for credit losses declined by $28.6 million due to primarily due to changes in estimates to property specific credit and performance metrics as well as changes in economic forecasts. Land rights and ground lease expense increased by $7.7 million due to the acquisition of assets in Bally's Master Lease II. General and administrative expenses increased by $3.9 million due primarily from an executive severance charge of $6.3 million, partially offset by lower stock based compensation expense of $3.1 million due primarily from forfeitures from the executive awards. During the year ended December 31, 2024, the Company recorded a gain of $3.8 million on the reclassification of the Tropicana Las Vegas Lease to a sales type lease from an operating lease due to a lease
reconsideration event. Finally, the Company incurred higher depreciation expense of $5.7 million due to its recent acquisitions.

•Other expenses, net increased by $28.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, as compared to the prior year. The increase was due to higher borrowing levels that partially funded our recent acquisitions, a decrease in interest income due to lower average interest earning balances in the current year. Additionally, results for the year ended December 31, 2025 included a debt extinguishment charge of $3.8 million for a call premium payment and accelerated amortization of debt issuance costs due to a senior unsecured note redemption.
•Net income increased by $42.7 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, as compared to the prior year, primarily due to the variances explained above.

paragraphs: GLPI 是一家自行管理與自行經營的賓州 REIT。GLPI 於 2013 年 2 月 13 日成立，為 PENN Entertainment, Inc.（原名為 Penn National Gaming, Inc.，於 NASDAQ 上市，代碼為 PENN（"PENN"））的 wholly-owned 子公司。2013 年 11 月 1 日，PENN 透過一系列內部公司重整程序，將與 PENN 的實物財產權益及不動產開發業務相關的資產與負債，以及 Hollywood Casino Baton Rouge 和 Hollywood Casino Perryville（簡稱為 "TRS Properties"）的資產與負債，轉讓給本公司，並隨後將 GLPI 以無稅方式分發給 PENN 普通股與優先股持有人（"Spin-Off"）。

自 2021 年起，本公司已設立為一個 umbrella partnership REIT，其業務幾乎全部透過 GLP Capital, L.P.（"GLP Capital"）進行。GLP Capital 的日常管理完全由 GLPI 控制。GLPI 除對 GLP Capital 的投資外，沒有其他重大資產。GLPI 會不定時發行權益，並有義務將這些發行所得淨資金轉賜給 GLP Capital。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，GLPI 持有 GLP Capital 97.1% 的單位，其餘單位由第三方有限合夥人持有，這些合夥人（直接或透過關係企業）以財產對 GLP Capital 進行投資，換取部分由發行經營合作單位（"OP Units"）及長期激勵計劃單位（"LTIP Units"）資助的對價。OP Units 和 LTIP Units 一旦解禁，可按一對一比例兌換為本公司普通股。本公司普通股於 NASDAQ 上上市，代碼為 GLPI。
本公司所有債務，包括循環信貸設施、定期貸款及高級無擔保債券，均由 GLP Capital 及其子公司發行。GLPI 已對本公司所有現有債務義務提供完全且無條件的擔保。
本公司旨在提供投資機會，以參與賭博產業的成長潛力，同時享有 REIT 的穩定性與現金流優勢。GLPI 的主要業務為取得、融資及擁有用以出租給賭博經營者之不動產，以 triple-net 租賃方式進行。本公司亦提供貸款，產生固定或變動回報，這些貸款在項目完工或穩定後，可能轉為租金。

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，GLPI 的資產組合包含 69 間賭博及相關設施的權益，包括 PENN 運營的 34 間賭博及相關設施的實物財產、Caesars Entertainment（於 NASDAQ 上市，代碼為 CZR）（"Caesars"）運營的 6 間賭博及相關設施的實物財產、Boyd Gaming Corporation（於 NYSE 上市，代碼為 BYD）（"Boyd"）運營的 4 間賭博及相關設施的實物財產、Bally's Corporation（於 NYSE 上市，代碼為 BALY）（"Bally's"）運營的 15 間賭博及相關設施的實物財產，以及正在開發中的 1 間設施 namely Bally's Chicago，Cordish Companies（"Cordish"）運營的 3 間賭博及相關設施的實物財產、由 Hard Rock International（"Hard Rock"）子公司管理的 1 間賭博設施、Strategic Gaming Management, LLC（"Strategic"）運營的 4 間賭博及相關設施的實物財產，以及 American Racing & Entertainment, LLC（"American Racing"）運營的 1 間賭博及相關設施的實物財產。這些設施，包括本公司總部大樓，地理分佈於 20 個州，本公司擁有超過 5,600 英畝土地，並租賃約 1,000 英畝土地。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司所有設施均為 100% 佔用。GLPI 預期會持續擴充其資產組合，透過尋找在合適條件下取得或開發更多賭博設施的機會，以出租給賭博經營者。
我們認為以下競爭優勢將對我們的成功有重大貢獻：
地理多樣化的不動產資產組合

我們透過與不同司法管轄區的多個租戶合作，來擴充我們的資產組合。我們主要聚焦於區域性賭博市場，這些市場的顧客較少依賴航空旅行，且需求歷來表現堅強。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們的資產組合包含 69 間賭博及相關設施。我們的資產組合，包括本公司總部大樓，約為 6,600 英畝土地，地理分佈於 20 個州，我們預期將擴展至 22 個州，因我們最近宣佈在加州和維吉尼亞州的交易。我們預期地理多樣化將限制任何一個區域市場下降對我們整體表現的影響。

本公司約 97% 的現金租金來自五家租戶 PENN、Caesars、Boyd、Cordish 和 Bally's，這些租戶為領導性、多元化、跨司法管轄區的賭場及賽馬場所有者與管理者，並為已建立的賭場服務提供者。除 Cordish 外，上述所有租戶皆為公開上市的公司，須遵守 1934 年證券交易所法案（經修正）的資訊申報要求，並須向證券交易委員會（"SEC"）提交定期報告 Form 10-K 和 Form 10-Q，以及現況報告 Form 8-K。讀者可至 PENN、Caesars、Boyd 和 Bally's 各自網站，以取得這些公司的進一步財務資訊。

本公司不動產資產透過長期三重淨租約出租，由租戶擔保，根據租約，租戶需承擔所有設施維護、與出租不動產相關的保險、以及在出租不動產上進行業務所需的保險，包括保障地主權益、出租不動產相關的稅務（不包括本公司所得稅）以及所有必需或適當的電力及其他服務。本公司租約包含固定 escalators、與達成特定租金覆蓋比率相關的 escalators，以及其他與租金成長相關的契約條款，例如與消費者物價指數（"CPI"）連結的 escalators，並設有上限與下限。
具備韌性的區域性賭場特性

本公司的資產組合主要由區域性、車程前往的賭場不動產組成，而非度假型賭場。從歷史表現來看，區域性賭場不動產的績效波動較小，相較於度假型賭場。此外，由於較低的資本支出負擔，區域性賭場資產在相同租金結構動態下，往往證明為更穩定的現金流來源。此外，我們認為 COVID-19 大流行所引發的經濟衰退已顯示區域性賭場市場的韌性。儘管本公司所有不動產在 2020 年 3 月中旬被要求關閉，本公司仍收到 2020 年應收的全部租金，包括租金減免。
透過資金承諾實現內在成長
本公司透過租約中的契約性租金 escalators、收購以及開發專案的資金投入來實現成長。自 2024 年 1 月 1 日起，本公司已完成總計 37 億美元的交易。詳見財務明細註釋第 11 項，以取得預期將為本公司未來成長機會做出貢獻的各種資金承諾清單。

The major factors affecting our results for the year ended December 31, 2025, as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, were as follows:', 'translated': '本公司於2025年12月31日財務年度報告總營業收入及營業運作所得為2,594.8 百萬美元及2,201.5 百萬美元，分別較2024年12月31日財務年度的2,531.5 百萬美元及2,130.7 百萬美元。影響本公司2025年12月31日財務年度結果之主要因素，與2024年12月31日財務年度相比，如下所述：'}

•總計來自不動產的收入為2025年12月31日財務年度1,594.8 百萬美元及2024年12月31日財務年度1,531.5 百萬美元。2025年12月31日財務年度來自不動產的總收入較2024年12月31日財務年度增加63.2 百萬美元。此增加主要係因本公司近期的收購及開發活動，整體使現金收入增加73.6 百萬美元。本年度結果亦受益於租賃契約的租金調整增加17.7 百萬美元，以及百分比租金增加2.3 百萬美元。本公司亦認列不當的直線租金及遞延租金調整項目為33.6 百萬美元，較前一年度同期減少，同時其對租賃投資的貼現減少0.6 百萬美元。最後，本公司有較高的土地租金收入3.9 百萬美元。

•總計營運費用於2025年12月31日財務年度較前一年度減少7.6 百萬美元。信用減損提撥減少28.6 百萬美元，主要係因對特定不動產信用及績效指標的預估變動，以及經濟預測的變動所致。土地權利及土地租賃費用增加7.7 百萬美元，係因收購Bally's Master Lease II的資產。一般及行政費用增加3.9 百萬美元，主要係因執行長離職補償費用6.3 百萬美元，部分抵銷因執行長獎勵計畫中獎勵未行使而導致的股票基於報酬費用減少3.1 百萬美元。於2024年12月31日財務年度，本公司因將Tropicana Las Vegas租賃契約從營運租賃重新分類為銷售型租賃，而確認收益3.8 百萬美元。
重新評估事件。最後，本公司因近期收購而產生較高的折舊費用，金額為 570 萬美元。
•其他費用，淨額於 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年較前一年增加 2800 萬美元。此增加係因較高的借款水準，部分用以資助我們近期的收購，以及因當年平均利息收入餘額較低，導致利息收入減少。此外，2025 年 12 月 31 日財年的結果包含因贖回高階無擔保票據而產生的債務消滅費用 380 萬美元，包含叫價支付及加速償還發行費用的折舊。
•淨收入於 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年較前一年增加 4270 萬美元，主要係因上述變動所致。

headings: 風險因素與我們的業務相關
我們任何租戶的破產或財務困難可能會導致該租戶終止租約，並對我們造成重大損失。
我們追求對更多不動產進行投資、收購或開發，可能無法成功或未能達成我們的預期。
我們依賴於賭博產業，可能面臨與此產業相關的風險，這些風險可能對我們的業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成重大不利影響。
我們部分租戶經營並管理的設施位於經歷極端天氣條件的地區，且對氣候變遷的負面影響較為敏感。
我們面臨來自賭博及其他監管機構的嚴格規範。
取得必要的監管許可可能延宕或禁止我們轉讓賭博不動產，這可能會導致我們在一段期間內無法收到這些不動產的租金。
我們與提供資金用於各類賭場開發專案的協議，使我們面臨與擁有及出租不動產不同的損失風險。
我們可能無法行使作為部落貸款貸款人之通常強制執行權。
我們追求與遊戲產業無關之戰略收購，可能無法成功或未達我們預期。
我們所擁有之不動產之環境合規成本及負債，可能對該投資之價值造成重大損害。
我們面臨因網路攻擊、網路入侵或其他方式之安全漏洞所導致之風險，以及資訊科技（IT）網路及相關系統之重大中斷風險。
我們面臨與我們之不動產有關之地面及使用租約之相關風險。
美國貿易政策及關稅之不確定性及變動，可能增加成本並對我們租戶之財務狀況造成不利影響，進而影響我們之財務狀況。
我們之成功取決於我們吸引、激勵及留住關鍵人員，並為未來高階主管轉換做準備之能力。
與我們作為REIT之地位相關之風險因素
符合 REIT 規定涉及美國稅法中高度技術性且複雜的條款，違反這些條款可能會影響我們的 REIT 資格。
我們可能無法符合被課徵 REIT 稅的條件，如果我們從租客或其子公司所獲得的收入未被視為符合條件的收入。
REIT 所發放的股息無法適用某些股息所享有的減稅率。
美國聯邦所得稅法的變更可能會對我們及我們的股東造成重大且不利的影響。
REIT 分配要求可能會對我們執行業務計畫的能力產生不利影響。
即使我們持續符合 REIT 資格，我們仍可能面臨其他稅務負擔，進而減少我們的現金流。
符合 REIT 要求可能會使我們放棄原本有吸引力的收購機會或清算原本有吸引力的投資。
符合 REIT 要求可能會限制我們有效進行避險的能力，並導致我們產生稅務負擔。
本公司章程限制本公司現有股票的所有權與轉讓，此舉可能導致延遲、推遲或防止本公司之交易或控制權變更。
與本公司資本結構相關之風險
本公司負有重大債務，此債務可能對本公司業務產生重大影響。
paragraphs: 本公司絕大多數的營業收入依賴 PENN 及其子公司。任何對 PENN 的業務、財務狀況或營運結果造成重大不利影響的事件，可能對本公司的業務、財務狀況或營運結果造成重大不利影響。

本公司絕大多數的營業收入係基於我們與 PENN 子公司簽訂的總體租賃契約所產生的收入。由於這些總體租賃契約為三重淨租賃，我們依賴 PENN 以產生足夠收入的方式運作我們所擁有的不動產，以使 PENN 能履行對我們的義務，包括支付租金及所有保險、稅務、電力、維護與修繕費用，並為我們賠償、辯護及確保我們免受與其業務相關的各種聲請、訴訟及負債的影響。無法保證 PENN 會有足夠的資產、收入或取得融資的管道，以履行其根據總體租賃契約對我們的付款義務。PENN 履行其義務的能力，部分取決於其賭博業務的總體獲利能力，除了我們作為出租人的有限契約保障外，我們對 PENN 或其業務毫無控制權。PENN 若無法履行其子公司租金義務及其他總體租賃契約義務，可能對本公司的業務、財務狀況或營運結果造成重大且不利的影響，包括我們支付股東紅利的能力。

由於我們對 PENN 的租金支付為重要收入來源，我們可能在執行總體租賃契約下的權利時受到限制。PENN 若未能遵守總體租賃契約條款或未能遵守所出租不動產所適用的賭博規範，我們可能需要尋找其他租賃人。在這種情況下，我們可能無法在相似租金率或任何條件下找到合適的租賃人，這將導致我們租金收入減少。同樣地，若 PENN 未能續約或延長任何總體租賃契約，且我們無法在經濟有利條件下出租或重新出租我們的不動產，我們的財務狀況可能受到重大影響。
任何對 PENN 的業務、財務狀況或營運結果造成重大不利影響的事件，包括公司控制權變更或 PENN 董事會成員組成的重大變動，可能對本公司的業務、財務狀況或營運結果造成重大不利影響。此外，賭博產業持續合併將增加我們對現有租戶的依賴，並使我們更難尋找替代租戶。

我們租戶的破產或財務困難可能降低我們從該租戶租賃所得的收入。若租戶破產或財務困難，聯邦法可能禁止我們僅基於該破產或財務困難而驅逐該租戶。此外，破產或財務困難的租戶可能被授權拒絕並終止與我們的租賃契約。針對該破產租戶未支付的未來租金的聲請，將受到法定限制，這將導致我們收到的租金收入大幅低於租賃契約中規定的應收租金。此外，我們對未支付過去租金的聲請可能無法獲得全部償還。我們也可能無法重新出租已終止或拒絕的空間，或在相同或更優厚的條件下重新出租。此外，考慮要申請破產保護的租戶可能要求修改其總體租賃契約，以將其租賃的不動產從我們的總體租賃契約中移除。我們無法保證我們能出售或重新出租這些不動產，或所收到的租賃終止費用（如有）足以彌補因租賃契約修改而導致的租金收入損失。

我們所處的產業為高度競爭性產業，面臨來自其他 REIT（包括其他專注賭博的 REIT）、投資公司、私人股權與對衝基金投資者、主權基金、貸款機構、賭博公司及其他投資者的競爭，其中一些機構規模較大、資源較多且資金成本較低。競爭增加可能使我們更難以識別並成功把握符合我們投資目標的收購機會。若我們無法識別並收購足夠數量的投資不動產或無法在商業上有利的條件下進行融資，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況或營運結果造成重大不利影響。此外，我們必須將 90% 的淨課稅所得分配以維持 REIT 資格，這可能限制我們依賴出租不動產或後續收購不動產的租金收入以進行收購。因此，若無法在可接受的條件下取得債務或權益融資，進一步收購可能受到限制或中止，並可能對擬議收購造成不利影響。此外，我們普通股價格的波動可能影響我們透過發行普通股進行進一步收購的能力，並可能導致重大稀釋。
